en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Seventh Chapter
The Discussion on Whether Earth is the Ripening of Karma:
Is earth the ripening of karma?
Yes, it is.
To be experienced as pleasant, to be experienced as painful, to be experienced as neither-painful-nor-pleasant;
associated with pleasant feeling, associated with painful feeling, associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling;
associated with contact, associated with feeling, associated with perception, associated with volition, associated with consciousness; having an object.
Is there, for that [feeling], turning toward it, attention, application of mind, mental attention, volition, aspiration, and resolve?
One should not say so... [etc. ...

Is it not the case that it is neither to-be-experienced-as-pleasant, nor to-be-experienced-as-painful, nor to-be-experienced-as-neither-painful-nor-pleasant, and is not for the sake of pleasant feeling?

They are not associated; they are not associated with painful feeling, not associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, not associated with contact, not associated with feeling, not associated with perception, not associated with volition, not associated with consciousness; they are without an object.
Is there no turning toward it, no inclination, no attention, no mental engagement, no volition, no aspiration, and no resolve regarding that?
Yes. If so, then it is neither to be experienced as pleasure nor to be experienced as pain... [and so on].
It is without an object;
there is in it no turning toward [objects], nor... nor aspiration. Indeed, it should not be said that "earth is the result of kamma."
Contact is the result of kamma; contact is to be experienced as pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant;
it is associated with pleasant feeling, associated with painful feeling... [and so on] ...associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling;
it is associated with contact, associated with feeling, associated with perception, associated with volition, associated with consciousness, and possesses an object.
Is there for it a turning toward [the object], and so forth, up to a mental aspiration? Yes.
Is earth the result of kamma, and is earth to be experienced as pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant?
Is that which is associated with pleasant feeling, or associated with painful feeling, or associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling;
which is associated with contact, associated with feeling, associated with perception, associated with volition, and associated with consciousness; which possesses an object;
and in which there is turning toward, mental advertence, attention, mental application, volition, aspiration, and resolve—[is this not so]?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is earth the result of kamma?
Is earth neither to be experienced as pleasant nor to be experienced as painful … [as before] … is it without an object?
Is there no turning toward it … [as before] … nor aspiration for it?
“Yes.
“Contact is a result of kamma; contact is neither to be experienced as pleasant nor to be experienced as painful … [and so on] … it is without an object;
there is no turning toward it … [and so on] … no aspiration for it? “Yes.”
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is earth the result of kamma? Yes.
Is earth subject to support and suppression, and subject to cutting and breaking? Yes.
Is the result of kamma subject to support and suppression, and subject to cutting and breaking?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it possible to buy, sell, barter, gather, or select earth? Yes.
Is it possible to buy, sell, barter, pluck, or select the ripening of karma?
One should not say so… [and so on]… Is earth common to others?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is the ripening of kamma shared with others?
You should not say so… [and so on].
Is the ripening of kamma shared with others?
Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One:
“A treasure not shared with others, a hoard that thieves cannot steal—
a mortal should perform meritorious deeds.”
“If one should practice good conduct.
Is this indeed a sutta? Yes.
In that case, it should not be said:
"The ripening of karma is common to others.
Is the earth the ripening of karma?
“Yes.
“Then is it the case that first the earth is established and afterwards sentient beings arise?
“Yes.”
“First the result arises, and afterwards one performs the karma for the sake of obtaining that result”?
One should not say so… [and so on]… Is the earth the result of the karma of all sentient beings?
“Yes.
“Then all beings enjoy the earth?
“One should not say that,” and so forth.
Do all beings enjoy the earth? Yes.
Are there any who attain final nibbāna without having enjoyed the earth? [No.]
“Yes,” you say.
“Are there some who attain final nibbāna without having exhausted the results of their kamma?
You must not say so … [and so on].
Is the earth the karmic result of the wheel-turning monarch?
Yes. Do other beings enjoy the earth? Yes.
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “Do other beings enjoy the karmic result of a wheel-turning monarch’s action? [The proponent replies:
“One must certainly not say so…” and so forth.
Do other beings enjoy the karmic result of the wheel-turning monarch’s being? Yes.
Do other beings enjoy the wheel-turning monarch’s contact, feeling, perception, volition, consciousness, faith, energy, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Should it not be said that “earth is the result of kamma”?
“Yes.
“Is it not the case that there is karma leading to sovereignty and karma leading to lordship?
“Yes.”
If there is indeed karma that leads to sovereignty and karma that leads to lordship, then, indeed, it must be said:
"The earth is the result of karmic fruition.
The discussion on whether the earth is the result of karmic fruition is concluded.
